title: Medical and Life-Support Protections: Practitioner Certification Requirements
content:
A protection under Medical and Life-Support Protections rests on a certification by a licensed practitioner. The practitioners whose certification is accepted, the treatment of telephone certification and the period within which a valid certification must be received differ by protection, as scheduled below.

## Accepted practitioners and license check

| Protection | Practitioners whose certification is accepted | License number check |
|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner, physician assistant or local board of health | license number checked against the state licensing board before registration |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner or physician assistant | license number checked against the state licensing board before registration |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner or physician assistant | license number checked against the state licensing board before registration |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner or physician assistant | license number checked against the state licensing board before registration |
| Life-Support Registration | physician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner or physician assistant | license number checked against the state licensing board before registration |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | physician (MD or DO) only | license number checked against the state licensing board before registration |

## Self-certification, telephone certification and time limits

| Protection | Customer's own statement accepted in place of a practitioner certification | Practitioner's telephone certification accepted pending the written form | Calendar days after a telephone certification for the written form to arrive | Calendar days after the application for a valid certification to be received |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | no | yes | 7 | 7 |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | no | no | 0 (telephone certification not accepted) | 30 |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | no | no | 0 (telephone certification not accepted) | 30 |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | no | no | 0 (telephone certification not accepted) | 30 |
| Life-Support Registration | no | yes | 7 | 30 |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | no | yes | 7 | 14 |

## Reading the schedule

- **Self-certification**: for every protection the answer is no — the customer's own statement is never accepted in place of a practitioner certification.
- **Telephone certification**: accepted pending the written form for the Medical Emergency Certificate, the Life-Support Registration and the Critical Care Life-Support Registration, each with 7 calendar days for the written form; not accepted for the three medical baseline allowances, where the follow-up figure is 0.
- **Who may certify**: a local board of health is an accepted certifier only for the Medical Emergency Certificate. A nurse practitioner or physician assistant is accepted for every protection except the Critical Care Life-Support Registration, which accepts a physician (MD or DO) only.
- **Certification period**: 7 calendar days for the Medical Emergency Certificate, 14 for the Critical Care Life-Support Registration and 30 for the other four protections.

### Hypothetical illustration

A nurse practitioner certifies a patient for the Critical Care Life-Support Registration. A nurse practitioner is not among the practitioners whose certification that protection accepts (physician, MD or DO, only), so the certification is not one from an accepted practitioner for that protection; the same nurse practitioner's certification is from an accepted practitioner for the Life-Support Registration.
